experiments.hypothesis: E01b as committed (e566234): the reference for every gate.
The -42 dBFS gate is a microphone-gain assumption. Removing it (level judged only against the noise floor) makes behaviour identical at any gain; the risk is new stops on quiet sounds in quiet rooms.

Silero VAD alone as the speech-frame test (same 200 ms in 300 ms rule, same -42 dBFS gate): rejects non-speech (cough, laugh, horn, noise steps) and bridges stop closures, but cannot tell an acknowledgement from an interruption.
TEN VAD alone under the same conditions as B1 (10 ms hops, no extra buffering).
E01b acoustic frames with neural confirmation: a STOP also needs 100 ms of Silero speech in the window. Keeps E01b's fast onset and noise-floor logic; the VAD only vetoes non-speech.

The agent channel is a clean reference: caller frames whose level follows the agent's level at a fixed delay are echo, not a caller. Should remove the speakerphone false stops without hiding a caller who talks over the echo.
The same echo gate on E01b without any neural model (is the echo gate useful on its own?).

Gain-invariant loudness: compare the evidence with the caller's own earlier speech level instead of an absolute level. Evidence more than 6 dB below it is 'soft' and must last 1000 ms in 1400 ms before a STOP. Acknowledgements are short and soft; a soft but sustained interruption is still caught, later.
With a caller-relative reference in place the absolute -42 dBFS gate should no longer be needed.

Silero speech frames + caller-relative loudness (soft tier 6 dB, 1000 ms in 1400 ms): the VAD removes non-speech and far-field sound, the caller reference handles soft acknowledgements. The two address different error classes, so the gains should add.
Sound more than 12 dB below the caller's own level is background (TV, another talker, echo) and should never stop the agent, however long it lasts.
The confirm-mode hybrid (E01b frames + VAD veto) with the caller reference, as an alternative to H1 that keeps the acoustic front end.

At -12 dB microphone gain H1 misses 4 xdev interruptions and one dev interruption: attenuated speech frames fall under the absolute -42 dBFS gate. With a neural VAD deciding what is speech and the caller reference judging loudness, the absolute gate is no longer needed; removing it should make the misses at low gain disappear without new false stops at normal gain.

A short word with a stop closure (توقف: 120 ms + 140 ms closure + 140 ms) never reaches 200 ms of speech inside 300 ms. A 400 ms window (200 ms = half) catches it. The 2/3 occupancy was there to stop sparse non-speech bursts adding up; the VAD now handles those.

Keep what the -42 dBFS gate does at nominal gain, but make it gain-invariant: once the caller's own level is known, a speech frame must be within 20 dB of it (the absolute gate only applies before the caller has spoken). Scores should then be the same at -12, 0 and +6 dB, and close to H1 at 0 dB.
On the gain-invariant detector: sound more than 12 dB below the caller's level is background (TV, another talker, echo) and never stops the agent.
400 ms evidence window (as W1) on the gain-invariant detector, for short words with a stop closure.

G2/W2 still miss interruptions at -12 dB because the caller reference is learned only from frames that already passed the absolute gate: with a quiet microphone it never becomes trusted and the absolute gate stays in force. Learning the reference from VAD speech frames before any loudness gate should remove those misses and make -12 / 0 / +6 dB behave alike.

The remaining low-gain miss (dev GI-D03 at -12 dB) is the VAD itself: Silero's output falls when the same audio is 12 dB quieter. Scaling the VAD input so that the caller's own level sits at a nominal -22 dB (gain limited to -12..+24 dB, only once the reference is trusted) should make the VAD see the same signal at any microphone gain.
Sensitivity of the soft-tier boundary: 4 dB instead of 6 dB. Expect more acknowledgements kept and more normal-level interruptions delayed (same-speaker words vary by about +/-5 dB).
Sensitivity of the soft-tier boundary: 8 dB instead of 6 dB. Expect fewer acknowledgements kept and no delayed interruptions.
